headline_marked: TSMC [[AI demand nearly doubles]] fab equipment needs, 2026 CapEx nears $64B
headline: TSMC AI demand nearly doubles fab equipment needs, 2026 CapEx nears $64B
summary: The world's largest chipmaker is drastically increasing its orders for manufacturing equipment, driven by an unprecedented surge in AI chip production. This has led to tool shortages across the industry.
details: TSMC has nearly doubled its projected requirements for semiconductor production equipment in just six months, according to deputy co-chief operating officer Cliff Hou. This surge is primarily driven by the escalating demand from the AI sector.

The foundry's equipment needs increased to 1.5 times its initial projection by the end of Q1 and then to 1.9 times by July, indicating a near doubling in demand for manufacturing tools within a short period.
TSMC attributes these increased needs to the construction of new fabs in Taiwan and the U.S., as well as upgrades to existing facilities, all of which require new machinery.

Despite the massive increase in equipment demand, TSMC's capital expenditure (CapEx) for 2026 has not risen proportionally. The projected CapEx for 2026 has been revised upwards from an initial $52-$56 billion to $60-$64 billion, a roughly 15% increase.

The foundry acknowledges that it cannot meet all customer demand but is working to scale up production capacity. The massive demand for wafer fab tools has also led to shortages across the industry, impacting all chipmakers.

headline_marked: [[Google Gemini]] misleads climbers, leading to mountain rescue
headline: Google Gemini misleads climbers, leading to mountain rescue
summary: Chatbot suggested an 8-hour trek for Mt. Shasta climb, resulting in a 16-hour ascent and a rescue operation by authorities.
details: A group of climbers attempting to scale Mount Shasta in California were forced to be rescued after relying on Google's Gemini chatbot for planning. The AI reportedly estimated the climb would take only eight hours, leading the unprepared group to pack insufficient food, water, and gear.

Gemini also advised the climbers to pack simple carbohydrates instead of fats, claiming fats "take too long to digest." This advice, combined with the inaccurate time estimate, meant the group carried only daypacks suitable for a short excursion, with no provisions for shelter or warm clothing.

The climbers set out at 3 AM and it took them 16 hours to reach the summit, by which time it was already 7 PM. This was well past the recommended turnaround time, and as they began their descent in darkness, they became lost.

Their phone, which was running the AllTrails navigation app, died, leaving them without a way to find their way down. They contacted 911 for assistance, but it took until the morning of August 31 for US Forest Service Climbing Rangers and the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office Search and Rescue team to reach them.

Due to weather conditions preventing a helicopter rescue, the stranded climbers had to descend on foot, a journey that took an additional nine hours. The climbers reportedly admitted to "relying too much on AI rather than our own critical thinking."

The Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office is now advising all climbers to contact the Mount Shasta Ranger station directly for the most accurate and up-to-date information and strongly recommends against relying solely on AI for critical planning.
